Day-of-year 312 sets ORDER only: group lead rotates so no group leads twice in a row (geopolitics led 11-06, policy_regulation led 11-07, so elections_public_opinion leads today, then geopolitics, then policy_regulation); within each group the list starts at offset 312 % group_size in pool order (elections 9 -> 6: platform AI labeling first; geopolitics 10 -> 2: sovereign AI first; policy 15 -> 12: AI 기본법 first). Queries were not checked with WebSearch (budget reserved for librarians); librarians should prefer outlet RSS/sitemap_news feeds over site: search for recency. Window: last brief was 2026-11-07, so items published 11-07 (after the prior harvest) through 11-08 are in scope. Context: Sunday in Korea / Saturday in the US, so expect few agency releases; weight Friday-late/Saturday US court orders and filings, Korean Sunday wire items (yna, etnews, zdnet.co.kr, digitaltoday), Asia-Pacific weekend items (India, Japan, Philippines), and EU pre-meeting papers. Upcoming hooks (only official documents are new, previews are not): informal European Council in Dublin on AI 2026-11-13; House China/Foreign Affairs/Intelligence closed briefing with Nvidia's Jensen Huang 2026-11-18; lame-duck Congress returns mid-November (NDAA AI provisions); Meta's new commercial terms on AI scraping take effect 2026-11-20 (Norway and Brazil courts already suspended them; UK CMA probe open); Delhi HC Kriti Sanon hearing 2026-12-10. In scope: bills introduced/marked up, agency rules/bulletins, court rulings and filings, regulator enforcement, export-control actions, official post-election after-action reports on AI-enabled interference, platform takedown reports. OUT of scope: who won, seat counts, polling, horse-race analysis, 'AI was the big issue of the midterms' commentary. Neutrality rule from sources.json applies: report decisions/filings/releases, attribute contested claims, no partisan framing.
